note: Strategy on CD127 × PD-1: (1) Find the dense CD127+ cluster on the right; events at CD127 below the left edge of this cluster (a sparse, scattered CD127- region) form the CD127- side. (2) Within the CD127+ cluster, locate the PD-1 density peak — use it as the horizontal threshold. Above the PD-1 peak = Th1_CD127p_PD1p (recently activated, still memory-competent Th1; upper-right). Below the PD-1 peak = Th1_CD127p_PD1n (resting homeostatic memory Th1; lower-right, the dominant population). (3) Apply the same PD-1 threshold to the sparse CD127- region: above the threshold = Th1_CD127n_PD1p (chronically-activated effector Th1; upper-left); below the threshold = Th1_CD127n_PD1n (terminally differentiated / post-effector Th1; lower-left). Parent caveat: this Th1 compartment includes the plastic CXCR3+CCR6+ Th1/17 subset.
tips: Th1 activation/exhaustion state (CD127 × PD-1 quadrants). Parent note: under the Step 6 definition, 'Th1' includes CXCR3+CCR6+ (Th1/17 plastic) events — distributions here reflect a mixture of classical Th1 and Th1/17. CD127 (IL-7Rα) is a homeostatic / memory-maintenance receptor; PD-1 marks activation, and at sustained high levels is associated with exhaustion-related phenotypes (PD-1 alone is not sufficient to define exhaustion). Th1_CD127p_PD1n: CD127+ PD-1-. Th1_CD127p_PD1p: CD127+ PD-1+. Th1_CD127n_PD1p: CD127- PD-1+. Th1_CD127n_PD1n: CD127- PD-1-. In-panel co-marker priors for orthogonal activation-axis refinement (currently unused): HLA-DR (canonical late activation), CD25 (early activation, IL-2Rα), CD69 (very early activation).
